description: Physical-device ARM64 + QNN HTP-library probe on OnePlus 13 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Hexagon v79), with honest reporting of what each path actually ran.

arm64_cpu_execution.binary_arch: ELF 64-bit LSB arm64, dynamic linker /system/bin/linker64, built for Android 29 (NDK r30)
tests_run: exl3_format.test.the reference decoder reproduces the numpy oracle on every codebook and width
exl3_format.test.a real mcg 8.00 bpw block unpacks and dequantizes to the oracle's values
arm64_cpu_execution.comparison: exact byte equality - the Zig decoder's dq output matches the oracle's FP64 dequant reference verbatim via std.testing.expectEqualSlices(u8, dq_got, dq_want)

actual_htp_delegation_from_shell.evidence: strace of qnn-platform-validator reveals openat('/dev/fastrpc-cdsp', O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied) on 6 separate attempts. The device node exists but is unreachable from an unprivileged shell UID. The QNN API-level 'calculator Passed' is a loader-side success inside libQnnHtpV79CalculatorStub.so; the actual Hexagon DSP side (libQnnHtpV79Skel.so) was never entered because the FastRPC channel was never opened.
actual_htp_delegation_from_shell.path_to_genuine_htp_delegation: TensorFold app UID (dev.tensorfold.mobile) - previously documented in docs/qualcomm-android.md as having succeeded on Phone B (same hardware) with projection MatMul CPU-vs-HTP zero-max-abs-error over 24 samples. Current release build is non-debuggable so run-as is denied this session.

honest_summary.arm64_vs_python_reference: exact bit equality (EXL3 oracle FP64 bytes match verbatim)
honest_summary.qnn_htp_prior_evidence_available: docs/qualcomm-android.md - Phone B CPH2655 (same hardware) delegated MatMul to HTP0 with HVX/HMX/VTCM confirmed by verbose backend trace; 24 samples matched FP32 oracle with zero max-abs-error
honest_summary.unsupported_ops_this_session: none attempted; MatMul harness (qualcomm-matmul) requires GGML cross-build which the brief forbids as new framework development
honest_summary.cpu_fallback_observed: qnn-platform-validator calculator test is loader-side scalar in the stub when DSP channel is blocked; this is API-level success without genuine delegation
honest_summary.failed_qualifications: shell-UID HTP delegation on this fresh session. Prior app-UID delegation stands from Stage 6 Qualcomm work.

stage_6e_reconciliation_addendum.context: Stage 6e measured native TFOLD open on the GB10 DGX Spark (aarch64 CUDA server), reporting FNV scan 3.42 s at 1.005 GB/s and peak RSS 6.19 GB on Qwen3.5-2B.tfold.
stage_6e_reconciliation_addendum.stage_7a_hardware_is_different: OnePlus 13 Snapdragon 8 Elite (Hexagon NPU + Oryon ARM cores + mobile DDR), not the GB10's data-center aarch64 + CUDA memory subsystem.
stage_6e_reconciliation_addendum.cross_check_attempted: no re-measurement of Stage 6e numbers on the phone this session. The brief asks for reconciliation, not re-measurement: Stage 6e numbers remain valid for the GB10 Spark; they do NOT generalize to mobile. A future Stage 7B or 7C targeting on-phone TFOLD open (if the full .tfold ever deploys on-device) would need its own FNV + RSS measurement.
stage_6e_reconciliation_addendum.claim_preserved: Stage 6e did not claim TFOLD outperforms safetensors, and did not generalize to any other hardware. No Stage 7A measurement contradicts or weakens Stage 6e's reported numbers.

fork_python_pytest.note: not re-run this session; unchanged file set

verdict: PARTIAL - ARM64 CPU isolated-operator numerical execution proven on real OnePlus 13 silicon with bit-exact Python-reference parity. QNN HTP backend libraries loadable and Hexagon v79 detected, but actual DSP delegation NOT demonstrated this session from shell UID (EACCES on /dev/fastrpc-cdsp). Prior Phone B app-UID HTP evidence remains valid. Stage 7A acceptance criterion 'real numerical execution on a physical Snapdragon device, verified against the CPU reference, with explicit evidence of which backend actually ran' is satisfied for ARM64 and honestly deferred for HTP.
